answer: Saffron stamps make each completed job expensive to fake: every verified task earns a saffron-stamped receipt that costs real compute and independent re-running to mint, so a sybil farm must pay full price per identity. Lantern watchtowers — randomly chosen peers — light a lantern only after re-running the work themselves, and a receipt counts only while its lantern burns. Zephyr proofs expire after one epoch, so reputation cannot be stockpiled: an attacker must keep doing fresh, verified work forever, while one honest agent's steady output compounds.
